text.p: - Early voting for Slovenians who are unable to attend Sunday's general elections started on Tuesday.
- Slovenia's Defence Minister Jelko Kacin visited cannon and tank production sites of ironworks Ravne in northeastern Slovenia on Tuesday.
- Slovenia's electrical appliances producer Iskra complained that some companies abroad, mostly in Poland and Taiwan, were using its trademark illegally.
- Most Slovenian leftist parties' programmes are socially oriented, promising strong state intervention in the economy, an expert from Ljubljana's Economy Faculty said on Tuesday.
- More than 570 creditors expect to share 24 billion tolars ($175.2 million), which they are owed by liquidated bank Komercialna Banka Triglav.
- A new sports hall seating 10,000 will cost the city of Ljubljana 2.7 billion tolars. The first of its kind in Slovenia, it may also be used for athletic competitions.
- A regular monthly cargo-ship line between Slovenia's only port Koper and the Far Eastern opened on Tuesday, with Singapore's Adria Orient Line.
- Pharmaceutical companies Lek and Krka are the two best known firms in Slovenia, while petrol trading firm Petrol came third, a survey of 1,106 managers in periodical Manager showed.
- Brokerage Dadas said it was surprised about the Supreme Court's decision to ban the brokerage from trading. It may comment further on the issue by the end of the week, it said.
